task: Find a FREE sub-hourly historical surface-obs feed for LFPB (Paris-Le Bourget), the exact station Polymarket's Paris high-temp ladder settles on (per ref/pmkt_settlement_basis.md, wunderground.com/history/daily/fr/bonneuil-en-france/LFPB).
verdict_tier: sub-hourly, MARGINAL tier per task rubric (30-min, not 10-min-or-better)
headline: LFPB issues genuine half-hourly (H:00 and H:30 UTC) automated METAR/AUTO reports, 48 obs/day, not just hourly (24/day). Verified via three independent free sources (IEM global ASOS mirror, NOAA aviationweather.gov, Ogimet) with an exact-match cross-checked raw METAR string. No auth, no rate-limit gate, >=164 days of retrievable history confirmed (likely years more, not exhaustively tested). Meteo-France's OWN official open-data channels (meteo.data.gouv.fr / data.gouv.fr) were checked first per task instruction and are a DEAD END for this station/variable: their bulk 'Donnees climatologiques de base - 6 minutes' dataset is PRECIPITATION ONLY (confirmed from the dataset description), and their finest bulk TEMPERATURE archive is 'Donnees climatologiques de base - horaires' (hourly only) -- genuinely sub-hourly official temperature bulk data does not exist as an anonymous open download. This finding mirrors the sibling London (EGLC) feedhunt: same winning source (IEM asos.py with report_type=3&4), same 48/day cadence, same report_type=3-only undercount bug in the prior repo script.

candidates_checked.name: Meteo-France official open data (meteo.data.gouv.fr / data.gouv.fr, 'Donnees climatologiques de base' family)
candidates_checked.status: CHECKED THOROUGHLY per task's explicit start-here instruction -- CONFIRMED NOT VIABLE for sub-hourly temperature
candidates_checked.reason: Enumerated the full Meteo-France organization dataset catalog on data.gouv.fr (123 datasets). The only genuinely 6-minute ('infra-horaire') bulk-downloadable dataset is 'Donnees climatologiques de base - 6 minutes' (and its 'stations complementaires' counterpart) -- confirmed from the dataset's own description ('pour le parametre precipitation au pas temps 6 minutes') that this is PRECIPITATION ONLY, not temperature. The finest bulk TEMPERATURE dataset in the same family is 'Donnees climatologiques de base - horaires' -- hourly, does not clear the sub-hourly bar. The separate 'Donnees d'observation des principales stations meteorologiques' (SYNOP) dataset is explicitly documented as 'Frequence : 3 h' -- coarser than hourly. Confirmed LFPB/Le Bourget IS a station Meteo-France tracks (id 95088001, WMO 07150, network pack 'RADOME') via the official station metadata list, so the gap is a genuine product-availability gap, not a station-coverage gap: Meteo-France's automated RADOME sensors DO measure temperature at high internal frequency, but that finer-than-hourly temperature stream is not exposed as an anonymous open bulk download -- only the derived hourly aggregate and the raw precipitation 6-min series are. A real-time/short-retention 6-min temperature tap may exist behind the newer 'portail-api.meteofrance.fr' Observation API, but that requires free account/API-key registration (out of scope to create in this session) and, being a real-time product, was not established to have >=90 days of retrievable HISTORY even if pulled -- flagged as an unverified possible upgrade path, not relied on.

auth_summary: No API key, no account, no login required for the winning feed (IEM asos.py) or its two cross-check sources (aviationweather.gov, Ogimet single-hour query). All three are anonymous HTTP GET. Meteo-France's own official open-data products (checked first, per task instruction) that would be needed for a finer-than-hourly TEMPERATURE feed are either not exposed at all as bulk anonymous downloads, or (the newer portail-api.meteofrance.fr Observation API, not established to carry sub-hourly temp or long history) require free account registration.
rate_limits_summary: No documented hard rate limit found for any of the three sources used. This session made ~9 sequential GET requests across IEM/aviationweather.gov/Ogimet/data.gouv.fr at roughly 1/sec with pauses, no throttling, no errors, no CAPTCHA. Continued politeness (sequential, ~1 req/sec, cache-then-reuse) recommended per GROUNDING.md non-negotiable #8.
licensing_summary: IEM: public redistribution of WMO GTS METAR traffic, no restrictive terms found on the request endpoint. Ogimet: states free for non-commercial/research use. aviationweather.gov: US government (NOAA) public data, no restriction. None of these are Meteo-France's own data product, but all three ultimately carry the same underlying LFPB-originated METAR/SPECI report -- the same station and same report family Polymarket's Wunderground settlement page itself scrapes, per ref/pmkt_settlement_basis.md's 14/14 (100%) IEM-vs-settled agreement finding for Paris. Meteo-France's own open data (Etalab open license, free, no restriction) was checked and found to lack a sub-hourly temperature product for this station -- so it is not the winning candidate here, but is noted as the highest-provenance source if a future account-gated integration (portail-api.meteofrance.fr) is worth pursuing for the 6-min RADOME sensor stream.
relevance_to_grounding_blocker: ref/GROUNDING.md and ref/pmkt_final_verdict.md's STILL-BLOCKED verdict cite 'hourly METAR... under-reports the diurnal peak by ~1h of temperature change' as the coverage blocker for the 5 non-US whitelist cities including Paris. This feedhunt found that LFPB specifically is NOT limited to hourly cadence on this same free IEM source -- the prior script's report_type=3-only query call undercounted it, identically to the already-found London case. Re-running the coverage/signal-fire analysis for Paris with the corrected report_type=3&4 (30-min) pull is a natural, cheap next step (now proven for 2 of the 5 non-US cities: London and Paris) that could partially narrow (not necessarily close) the 74% no-signal-fired gap for these cities -- flagged for a follow-up study, not claimed as resolved here.
